sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and logging setup
sections.what: Loads the web tools, the orchestrator agent and the settings, and sets up logging for this file.
sections.why: Likely reason: logging lets the team trace what each workflow step did.
sections.watch_out: The server log is the first place to look when these routes fail.

sections.name: DiscoverRequest
sections.title: Request shape for discovery
sections.what: Holds just a company name for the discovery routes.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The quick model route reuses this same shape.

sections.name: AssumptionsRequest
sections.title: Request shape for assumptions
sections.what: Holds the company profile and the comparables data, both as free-form dictionaries.
sections.why: Likely reason: these come from earlier steps and their exact shape can change.
sections.watch_out: Whatever the caller sends is passed on without checks.

sections.name: discover_company
sections.title: Discovering a company
sections.what: Runs two steps in order: first a company profile, then comparables and benchmarks. Returns them together.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The two agent calls run one after the other, so a slow web search slows the whole request.

sections.name: determine_assumptions
sections.title: Setting model assumptions
sections.what: Turns the profile and comparables into a full set of model assumptions backed by research, so the user can review and edit them before building.
sections.why: Likely reason: the docstring says the user reviews assumptions first, which is why this is a separate step.
sections.watch_out: The assumptions are only as good as the research behind them, so the user should check the numbers.

sections.name: BuildModelRequest
sections.title: Request shape for building a model
sections.what: Holds the profile, the assumptions and the number of years, which defaults to 5.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The year count is not limited here.

sections.name: build_progressive_model
sections.title: Building the full model
sections.what: Builds the three-statement model from the profile and assumptions over the chosen years, and returns it with its formulas and steps.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Assumption names must match what the agent expects, or the build may fail or leave gaps.

sections.name: build_quick_model
sections.title: Quick test model
sections.what: Builds a five-year model for a company name using fixed starting numbers, not the company's own data.
sections.why: Likely reason: the docstring says it is a simplified endpoint for testing.
sections.watch_out: The model looks like a real forecast but uses the same starting revenue and growth for every company.

summary: Routes that run the whole modeling workflow in steps: discover a company, set its assumptions, build a model, and build a quick test model with fixed numbers.
purpose: Let the user type a company name and get a profile, comparable companies, benchmarks, assumptions and a finished model.
why: Likely reason: replaces the older question-and-answer process, as the discovery docstring says.
how: Discover asks the orchestrator agent for a profile, then finds comparables and benchmarks. Assumptions turns the profile and comparables into numbers. Build model creates a model over a number of years from those assumptions. Quick model uses hardcoded assumptions and the company name only.
inputs: A company name; profile and comparables dictionaries; an assumptions dictionary and a year count defaulting to 5.
outputs: A success status with the profile, comparables, benchmarks, assumptions or model.
risks: The quick model builds from invented numbers, not the company's data. Web research results may be outdated or wrong, and nothing here checks them.
debug: If discovery fails, check the orchestrator agent and the AI provider setting. Errors are logged with full traces in the server log, so start there.
